question: List all products.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM products;

question: List all products in the 'Electronics' category.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM public.products WHERE category = 'Electronics';

question: Find all products priced above 100 dollars.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM public.products WHERE price > 100;

question: Show all products in the 'Home & Kitchen' category ordered by price from highest to lowest.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM public.products WHERE products.category = 'Home & Kitchen' ORDER BY products.price DESC;

question: Retrieve all customers who live in the state 'CA'.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE state = 'CA';

question: Get all orders with status 'delivered'.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered';

question: List all order items for the laptop product whose name starts with 'Laptop Pro 15'.
expected_sql: SELECT oi.* FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.product_name LIKE 'Laptop Pro 15%';

question: Show all product reviews with a rating of 5.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM reviews WHERE rating = 5;

question: Get the distinct product categories available in the catalog.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products;

question: Count the total number of orders.
expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders;

question: List all customers whose email address ends with '@gmail.com'.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE email LIKE '%@gmail.com';

question: Find all products that are currently out of stock.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM products WHERE stock_quantity = 0;

question: Get all orders placed after 2024-01-20.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date > '2024-01-20';

question: List all order items where the quantity is greater than 1.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE quantity > 1;

question: Find the average rating for the laptop product whose name starts with 'Laptop Pro 15'.
expected_sql: SELECT AVG(rating) FROM reviews r JOIN products p ON r.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.product_name LIKE 'Laptop Pro 15%';

question: Retrieve all customers who live in the city 'New York'.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'New York';

question: List all products with a price between 40 and 100 dollars (inclusive).
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM public.products WHERE price BETWEEN 40 AND 100;

question: Find the single most expensive product.
expected_sql: SELECT products.product_name FROM products ORDER BY products.price DESC LIMIT 1;;

question: Show each product that has been ordered and the total quantity ordered for that product.
expected_sql: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_ordered FROM public.products AS p JOIN public.order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity_ordered DESC;

question: List all orders together with the first and last name of the customer who placed each order.
expected_sql: SELECT o.order_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;

question: For each order, show the order id and the total order amount using the order item subtotals.
expected_sql: SELECT order_id, SUM(subtotal) AS total_amount FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id;

question: List all products whose name contains the word 'Pro'.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM public.products WHERE product_name LIKE '%Pro%';

question: Show all customers ordered by last name in ascending order.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM customers ORDER BY last_name ASC;

question: Get all orders that have a non-empty notes field.
expected_sql: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE notes IS NOT NULL;

question: List all reviews with rating 4 or higher for products in the 'Electronics' category.
expected_sql: SELECT r.* FROM reviews r JOIN products p ON r.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND r.rating >= 4;

question: Calculate the total revenue generated from all order items.
expected_sql: SELECT SUM(subtotal) FROM order_items;

question: For each order, show the order id and total order amount, but only include orders with a total greater than 200.
expected_sql: SELECT order_id, SUM(subtotal) AS total_amount FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING SUM(subtotal) > 200;

question: Find customers who have placed more than one order and show how many orders each has placed.
expected_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 1;

question: List all products that have never been ordered.
expected_sql: SELECT p.* FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id);

question: Find the top 3 most frequently ordered products by total quantity ordered.
expected_sql: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity DESC LIMIT 3;

question: For each customer, show the total amount they have spent, but only include customers who have spent more than 200 in total.
expected_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING SUM(oi.subtotal) > 200;

question: List products that have at least two reviews and show their average rating.
expected_sql: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(r.review_id) >= 2;

question: Find customers who have never placed any orders.
expected_sql: SELECT c.* FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;

question: For each product category, show how many products belong to that category.
expected_sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products GROUP BY category;

question: For each order, show the number of order items and the total quantity ordered, but only for orders with more than one item in total.
expected_sql: SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS line_count, SUM(quantity) AS total_quantity FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING SUM(quantity) > 1;

question: List all products in the 'Electronics' category that have at least one review with rating 5.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND r.rating = 5;

question: Show all orders with their total order amount and status, ordered from highest to lowest total amount.
expected_sql: SELECT o.order_id, o.status, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS order_total FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id, o.status ORDER BY order_total DESC;

question: For each product category, find the average price, but only include categories where the average price is greater than 100.
expected_sql: SELECT category, AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING AVG(price) > 100;

question: Find all customers who have ordered at least one product from the 'Home & Kitchen' category.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Home & Kitchen';

question: List all products that have been ordered at least once but do not have any reviews.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name FROM products p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.product_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reviews r WHERE r.product_id = p.product_id);

question: Show the earliest and latest order dates in the system.
expected_sql: SELECT MIN(order_date) AS earliest_order_date, MAX(order_date) AS latest_order_date FROM orders;

question: For each city, show how many customers live there, but only include cities with at least two customers.
expected_sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY city HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

question: List all customers who have written at least one review and show how many reviews each has written.
expected_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(r.review_id) AS review_count FROM customers c JOIN reviews r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name;

question: For each product category, show the total quantity of items ordered from that category.
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

question: Find all orders that include at least one product from the 'Sports & Outdoors' category.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.status FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Sports & Outdoors';

question: For each order status, calculate the total revenue from orders with that status.
expected_sql: SELECT o.status, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.status;

question: Find customers who have both placed at least one order and written at least one review.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN reviews r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id;

question: For each rating value, show how many reviews have that rating.
expected_sql: SELECT rating, COUNT(*) FROM reviews GROUP BY rating;

question: List all products that have a stock quantity greater than 100 and that have been ordered at least once.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.* FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE p.stock_quantity > 100;

question: For each customer who has placed at least one order, show the date of their most recent order.
expected_sql: SELECT c.*, MAX(o.order_date) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name;

question: Find the top 3 customers by total amount spent on all their orders.
expected_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 3;

question: For each product that has been ordered show product name total quantity ordered total revenue and its percentage of overall revenue.
expected_sql: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_revenue, SUM(oi.subtotal) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(subtotal) FROM order_items) AS revenue_percent FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name;

question: List products whose average review rating is higher than the overall average rating across all reviews.
expected_sql: SELECT p.product_name, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING AVG(r.rating) > (SELECT AVG(rating) FROM reviews);

question: For each state show how many distinct customers have placed orders and the total revenue from that state only including states with revenue greater than zero.
expected_sql: SELECT c.state, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS customer_count, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.state HAVING SUM(oi.subtotal) > 0;

question: For each product category show how many distinct customers have ordered products in that category only including categories with at least two such customers.
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) >= 2;

question: Find customers who have written reviews for products that they themselves ordered.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c JOIN reviews r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id JOIN products p ON r.product_id = p.product_id JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id AND o.customer_id = c.customer_id;

question: Find customers with gmail addresses who have never placed any orders and have never written any reviews.
expected_sql: SELECT c.* FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id LEFT JOIN reviews r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id WHERE c.email LIKE '%@gmail.com' AND o.order_id IS NULL AND r.product_id IS NULL;

question: For each product that has been ordered show its name total quantity ordered and average review rating if it has reviews.
expected_sql: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name;

question: For each customer who has placed at least one order show only their most recent order and the total amount of that order.
expected_sql: SELECT customer_id, order_id, order_date, order_total FROM (SELECT o.customer_id, o.order_id, o.order_date, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS order_total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.order_date DESC, o.order_id DESC) AS rn FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.customer_id, o.order_id, o.order_date) t WHERE rn = 1;

question: List products whose total ordered quantity is greater than the average total ordered quantity across all ordered products.
expected_sql: SELECT product_name, total_quantity FROM (SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name) t WHERE total_quantity > (SELECT AVG(total_quantity) FROM (SELECT SUM(oi2.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p2 JOIN order_items oi2 ON p2.product_id = oi2.product_id GROUP BY p2.product_id) q);

question: For every customer show how many orders they have and how much they have spent in total including customers with no orders and sort by total spent descending.
expected_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count, COALESCE(SUM(oi.subtotal), 0) AS total_spent FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC;

question: Find the top 3 states ranked by total revenue generated from customers in those states.
expected_sql: SELECT c.state, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.state ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 3;

question: For each product category that has generated revenue show the total revenue and the average review rating for products in that category.
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_revenue, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.subtotal) > 0;

question: Find customers who have written five star reviews for more than one distinct product and show how many such products they reviewed.
expected_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT r.product_id) AS five_star_products FROM customers c JOIN reviews r ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id WHERE r.rating = 5 GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.product_id) > 1;

question: For each product show its price and the difference between its price and the average price of products in the same category.
expected_sql: SELECT product_id, product_name, category, price, price - AVG(price) OVER (PARTITION BY category) AS price_diff_from_category_avg FROM products;

question: List all products whose price is the maximum price within their own category.
expected_sql: SELECT p.* FROM products p WHERE p.price = (SELECT MAX(p2.price) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category = p.category);

question: Find customers whose total spending is above the average spending among all customers who have placed at least one order.
expected_sql: SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name, total_spent FROM (SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name) t WHERE total_spent > (SELECT AVG(customer_total) FROM (SELECT SUM(oi2.subtotal) AS customer_total FROM customers c2 JOIN orders o2 ON c2.customer_id = o2.customer_id JOIN order_items oi2 ON o2.order_id = oi2.order_id GROUP BY c2.customer_id) x);

question: For each calendar day show how many orders were placed and the total revenue for that day ordered by date.
expected_sql: SELECT DATE(o.order_date) AS order_day, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY DATE(o.order_date) ORDER BY order_day;

question: List all distinct pairs of different products that were ordered together in the same order.
expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT LEAST(p1.product_name, p2.product_name) AS product_a, GREATEST(p1.product_name, p2.product_name) AS product_b FROM order_items oi1 JOIN order_items oi2 ON oi1.order_id = oi2.order_id AND oi1.product_id < oi2.product_id JOIN products p1 ON oi1.product_id = p1.product_id JOIN products p2 ON oi2.product_id = p2.product_id;

question: For each order show its total amount and classify it as high if the total is at least 200 otherwise low.
expected_sql: SELECT o.order_id, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_amount, CASE WHEN SUM(oi.subtotal) >= 200 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS amount_category FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id;

question: Find the customer who placed the earliest order and show that order id order date and total amount.
expected_sql: SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, o.order_date, SUM(oi.subtotal) AS total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_date = (SELECT MIN(order_date) FROM orders) GROUP BY o.order_id, c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, o.order_date;

question: For each product show how many distinct customers both ordered and reviewed that same product.
expected_sql: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(DISTINCT r.customer_id) FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id AND o.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY p.product_name;

question: List product categories where the total stock quantity across all products in that category is greater than 300.
expected_sql: SELECT category FROM products GROUP BY category HAVING SUM(stock_quantity) > 300;

question: Find customers who live in a city and state where at least one customer has placed an order but who themselves have never placed any orders.
expected_sql: SELECT c.* FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM customers c2 JOIN orders o2 ON c2.customer_id = o2.customer_id WHERE c2.city = c.city AND c2.state = c.state);

question: For each product category that has reviews show the average review rating and order the results from highest to lowest average rating.
expected_sql: SELECT p.category, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating  FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY avg_rating DESC;
